PASS-1 (E4) assumption-verification note. Two load-bearing plan assertions about the `PeerConfirmationStore.record()` contract are refuted by the current `peer_confirmations.py`:

1. Scope directs `backfill_from_managed_refs(store, local_tickets, binding_store, pass_id) -> int`, but the landed function (peer_confirmations.py:278) has NO `pass_id` parameter — signature is `(store, local_tickets, binding_store) -> int`.

2. Scope directs writing a record with `confirmed_pass=pass_id`, `confirmed_at=<now ns>`. The current `record()` (peer_confirmations.py:144) has NO `confirmed_pass`/`confirmed_at` params — they were deliberately dropped (bug 266c / epic 0303 churn discipline, docstring lines 160-169) because they had no production reader and rewrote the whole sidecar every pass. The record carries `first_confirmed_at` (set once, then preserved) instead.

The Scope's field/parameter list should be reconciled with the current `record()` contract (drop `pass_id` from the signature and drop `confirmed_pass`/`confirmed_at` from the written fields). All other codebase assertions verified clean: `managed_ref_set` / `MANAGED_REF_KINDS` (`_managed_refs.py:50`), `binding_store.get_jira_key` (binding_store.py:195), `store.was_absent` (peer_confirmations.py:103), `is_confirmed()` acceptance of any recorded key (line 136), and the `_persist_and_log` seam existence.
